endorsements.quote: It is imperative to note that AI tools should always act as auxiliary aids to a physician.
At the current level of development, they cannot be used as autonomous decision-making tools.
Taking informed consent from patients is vital, as they deserve to understand how AI influences their medical care and outcomes.
Lastly, proper tuning and rigorous real-life testing of AI tools are necessary before introducing them to ensure diagnostic accuracy.

unlisted_practices: Develop explainable AI models to overcome the lack of transparency in decision-making algorithms.

Foster interdisciplinary collaboration among neurosurgeons, data scientists, AI experts, ethicists, and regulatory bodies to form guidelines and standards for ethical deployment of AI tools in patient care.
Conduct more research to advance AI capabilities and address limitations in glioblastoma diagnosis and management.

screen.reason: Editorial commentary discussing the applications, challenges, ethical considerations, and deployment needs of AI in glioblastoma diagnosis and care.
